message.content:
### Your Rights as a Tenant in Texas (as of 2024) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • The landlord may hold a maximum of **one month’s rent** (or two if the lease is for a month‑to‑month tenancy).
• The deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any move‑in inspection report.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if the landlord withholds part of the deposit. | | **Habitability** | • The landlord must keep the premises in a **safe, sanitary, and livable condition** (e.g., functioning plumbing, heating, electrical, pest control).
• Repairs that affect health or safety must be made promptly. | • Notify the landlord in writing (email or certified mail) of needed repairs.
• If the landlord fails to act, you may:
 • Withhold rent (after giving notice),
 • Make the repair yourself and deduct the cost from rent (after giving notice),
 • File a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) or local code enforcement. | | **Rent Payment & Late Fees** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are allowed only if the lease states them; they must be reasonable (no more than 5% of the monthly rent). | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan if you’re having trouble.
• Keep receipts or bank records of payments. | | **Entry & Privacy** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies.
• “Reasonable” means a time that is convenient for both parties. | • Ask for a written notice of entry.
• If the landlord enters without notice, you can refuse entry and document the incident. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR) or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Lease Termination** | • **Month‑to‑month**: Either party may terminate with **30 days’ written notice**.
• **Fixed‑term**: The lease ends on the date specified unless renewed.
• Early termination may be possible if the landlord breaches the lease (e.g., fails to maintain habitability). | • Provide written notice.
• Keep copies of all correspondence. | | **Rent Increase** | • For month‑to‑month leases, the landlord must give **30 days’ written notice** before raising rent.
• For fixed‑term leases, rent can only increase at the start of a new term unless the lease allows it. | • Review the lease for any rent‑increase clauses.
• Negotiate or seek legal advice if you believe an increase is unlawful. | | **Eviction** | • The landlord must follow the Texas **eviction process**: serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for nonpayment, 30‑day notice for lease violation).
• The landlord cannot evict you without a court order. | • Respond to notices promptly.
• Attend any court hearing.
• Seek legal aid if you’re facing eviction. | | **Repair & Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major defect, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, **provided** you give written notice and keep receipts. | • Document the defect, send notice, keep receipts, and calculate the deduction. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live in the property without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • Report any harassment or disturbances to the landlord in writing. | | **Insurance** | • While not required by law, it’s wise to have renter’s insurance covering personal property and liability. | • Obtain a policy that meets your needs. | | **Legal Assistance** | • Texas offers free or low‑cost legal services for tenants (e.g., Texas Legal Services Center, local bar association referral services). | • Contact a local tenant advocacy group or legal aid office. | --- #### Quick Checklist Before Moving In 1. **Read the Lease Thoroughly** – Pay special attention to: - Security deposit amount and conditions for return. - Notice periods for entry, rent increases, and termination. - Pet policies, subletting rules, and maintenance responsibilities. 2. **Document the Condition** – Take photos or videos of the unit’s condition before you move in. Keep a copy of the move‑in inspection report. 3. **Know Your Local Ordinances** – Some cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas) have additional tenant protections beyond state law. 4. **Keep All Records** – Store copies of rent receipts, maintenance requests, correspondence, and any notices received. --- #### When Things Go Wrong | Issue | First Step | Next Step | |-------|------------|-----------| | Landlord refuses to make repairs | Send a written notice (email or certified mail) detailing the problem and requesting repair. | If no response in 7–10 days, consider filing a complaint with TDHCA or local code enforcement. | | Unlawful rent increase | Verify the lease terms. If the increase violates the lease or notice requirements, refuse to pay the extra amount. | Seek mediation or legal advice. | | Eviction notice received | Review the notice for proper legal grounds and notice period. | File a response in court and consult a tenant lawyer. | | Discrimination claim | Gather evidence (emails, photos, witnesses). | File a complaint with TCHR or HUD. | --- #### Resources - **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)** – [https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us](https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us) - **Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR)** – [https://www.tchr.texas.gov](https://www.tchr.texas.gov) - **U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)** – [https://www.hud.gov](https://www.hud.gov) - **Texas Legal Services Center** – [https://www.texaslegalservices.org](https://www.texaslegalservices.org) - **Local Tenant Advocacy Groups** – Search online for “tenant rights Texas” + your city. --- **Bottom line:** As a Texas tenant, you have the right to a safe, habitable home, fair handling of your security deposit, reasonable notice for entry, protection against discrimination, and a clear, lawful eviction process. Keep detailed records, communicate in writing, and don’t hesitate to seek legal help if your landlord violates your rights.
